summary:
✅ Risk Score: LOW (10/100)

2 Medium

Review completed with 2 findings across 2 agents (2 medium).

findings.title: Log Injection vulnerability in BaseGeometryWidget
findings.description: This diff reverts a security fix for CVE-2026-111211. The new code uses `logger.error(..., value, err)` directly without using the `trim_value` utility or escaping the input. Since `value` comes from user input in the form widget, it is untrusted. If the user submits a geometry string containing newline characters (`\n`, `\r`) or ANSI escape sequences, these will be written directly into the logs. This enables log injection and log forgery, allowing an attacker to manipulate the structure of the application logs or inject fake log entries, which can be exploited to bypass security monitoring or hide malicious activity.
findings.suggestion: Restore the previous implementation that sanitized the value before logging. Use the `trim_value` utility from `django.utils.text` (or equivalent escaping logic) to escape control characters and limit the length of the logged value. Do not log raw user input directly into the log handler.

findings.title: Missing log trimming for large values causes excessive log volume
findings.description: The change removes the call to `trim_value` and directly logs the raw `value` variable. If the input `value` is extremely large (e.g., several megabytes of text or binary data), this will be written directly into the log file, potentially consuming excessive disk space or causing performance issues due to I/O blocking. Additionally, while the diff removes `log_message` to fix log injection (by not interpolating the value into the log string literal in a way that might be vulnerable if `value` contained newlines), using `logger.error` with `%s` formatting is the correct way to avoid log injection. However, the lack of trimming is a regression in log management.
findings.suggestion: Re-introduce trimming logic or a length limit when logging the value. For example, you can slice the value before logging: `value_to_log = value[:100] + '...' if len(value) > 100 else value`. This prevents log flooding while maintaining the security fix for log injection by ensuring the value is passed as an argument to the logger (which handles escaping in standard logging configs if needed, though `%s` is safe from injection in the log record structure itself, it is not safe from visual confusion if the value contains newlines). Actually, `logger.error` with lazy evaluation (passing `%s` and args) is safe from *injection* into the log structure, but if `value` contains newlines, it will span multiple lines in the log file. To mitigate this, escape newlines or truncate.
